design: Repeated-object learning in one continuous directed graph
primary: Actual first return to A after learning K distinct intervening objects, K=0,1,2,4,8,16, versus equal elapsed neutral activity and matched exposure without writes.
From the same pre-probe snapshot, score both A and B without intervening A/B feedback. Keep all sampled motor outcomes.
One jointly trained checkpoint on held-out continual visits, including worst mark/context law per individual and feedback-dependent action contrast.
evaluation: Cross hidden assignment with public geometry and left/right layout, reserve held-out tapes; sample training births as the independent units, not contacts. Show per-birth results and effect sizes.
credit: Train only from the physically realized resource of the chosen action. Give no correct-side labels or privileged address to the graph.
mechanistic_diagnosis: Vary angle between two odor directions at fixed duration. Cross whether their good directions agree. Compare native B write against same-prefix sham, targeted rollback of opposing versus dose-matched random surviving weights, and one real review of A versus equal-time exposure. Test both objects from identical pre-probe states.
decision: If learning B markedly erases A, prioritize interference and matched real review. If trained graphs retain both, prioritize capacity, long gaps and new context/layout transfer. Distinguish visible conflicts from unsignaled reversals, the latter only causally solvable after feedback.
scope: Within-session overnight research, local raw artifacts. Previously published repository remains the baseline.
